title: Improving Group Robustness on Spurious Correlation via Evidential Alignment

problem.claim: Deep neural networks may rely on spurious correlations, which can reduce generalization in diverse scenarios and challenge out-of-distribution robustness and trustworthiness.

gap.claim: Existing mitigation methods typically require costly external group annotations or auxiliary deterministic models that may not capture the full spectrum of learned biases.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes Evidential Alignment, a framework that uses uncertainty quantification to understand biased-model behavior without group annotations.
The framework combines second-order risk minimization for quantifying prediction evidence with evidential calibration to identify and suppress spurious correlations while preserving core features.
The paper theoretically justifies learning biased-model patterns and debiasing without spurious-correlation annotations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Evidential Alignment as a novel framework.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that empirical results significantly improve group robustness across diverse architectures and data modalities.

narrative_sequence.summary: Models learn superficial non-causal associations, causing weaker generalization when those associations fail.
Spurious correlations create challenges for out-of-distribution robustness and trustworthiness.
Existing approaches depend on costly group annotations or potentially incomplete deterministic bias models.
Evidential Alignment uses uncertainty quantification, second-order risk minimization, and evidential calibration to detect and suppress spurious correlations.
The paper provides a theoretical justification and reports empirical improvements in group robustness.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, architectures, data modalities, baselines, metrics, or numerical results.
The abstract does not provide details of the theoretical assumptions or proof.
